operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple ASCII, no spaces/mixed case; but spec still requires double-quoting and case-insensitive column lookup.
Tiny DB (8/13/7/14 rows) — no huge-table sampling path exercised; original_values fully read.
All declared types are INTEGER/TEXT; no Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year dispatch, no crash-fallback types.
All columns notnull=0 despite being PKs — sqlite PK on INTEGER is not NOT NULL; TS may insert NULL PKs and they fail at insert.
Authorship has composite PK (authID,instID,paperID) — composite-PK members get max_l0=30 cap in TS.
Authorship.authID/instID/paperID are both PK members and FK children — FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered column.
All FKs resolve to existing parents (parent_exists true); no dangling FKs, no self-references.
Parent PKs are single-column INTEGER with distinct=rows (no duplicates) — FK draws with replacement will still create duplicate Authorship rows, dropped by composite-PK dedup.
authOrder INTEGER distinct=3 (values 1,2,3) — Number fuzzer will produce values far outside [1,3].
Storage classes match declared types everywhere (integer/text); no contradictions.
No views, triggers, indexes beyond PKs in DDL.
TEXT columns hold multi-word strings with spaces, colons, periods (titles truncated mid-word) — String fuzzer's CHARSET lacks ':' and '.'.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INTEGER columns: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none -> default), then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs get fresh draws (max_l0=inf).
String fuzzer on name/country/lname/fname/title: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length [0,20], 50% contaminate; will not reproduce 'University of Oxford' style.
Literal pool from train SQL likely seeds country values (UK/USA/Japan/France) and maybe names — String sampler returns elements w.p. 1-p.
authOrder will be random large ints, not 1..3 — plausible FN source for queries filtering authOrder=1.
FK consistency: Authorship.authID/instID/paperID drawn from parent final values, so joins work; but composite-PK dedup drops many rows, shrinking Authorship.
Table sizes: level-based (Inst/Authors/Papers level 0, Authorship level 1) or rand_lin — Authorship ~4x parents, so many duplicate (authID,instID,paperID) triples dropped.
No NOT NULL enforcement: NULL PKs possible on Inst/Authors/Papers (INTEGER PK allows NULL in sqlite) — insert may succeed with NULL PK, creating odd states.
Missing ties/duplicates: original has distinct=rows on all PKs, so TS-generated duplicates are dropped — queries relying on duplicate rows (e.g. COUNT DISTINCT vs COUNT) may FP.
Implausible values: country gets random strings not in {UK,USA,Japan,France} — queries filtering country='USA' may FN if pool didn't seed it.
Titles truncated in original; TS random titles won't match LIKE patterns on real title substrings — FN for title LIKE queries.
Small DB means TS sizes (30-2500) vastly exceed original — cardinality-sensitive queries (e.g. HAVING COUNT>10) may flip.
